groups.title: Air Nation
groups.def: Members of Tenzin's Air Nation community (not just anyone who happens to airbend — this excludes airbenders like Zaheer who aren't part of it).

groups.title: Team Avatar
groups.def: The official core of Korra's Team Avatar and its two animal members, not counting the many characters who temporarily tag along for one arc.

groups.title: Waterbenders
groups.def: Every non-Avatar character shown waterbending in the show. Hasook plays pro-bending as the Fire Ferrets' waterbender; Viper waterbends in "The Sting". Senna is called a waterbender only in press material and never bends; Shady Shin's waterbending appears only in the Republic City Hustle web shorts.

groups.title: Firebenders
groups.def: Every non-Avatar firebender: characters shown firebending in this show (Zolt at Amon's rally, Zuko's dragon Druk breathing fire at the North Pole), plus Iroh, the original series' firebender, seen here only as a spirit.

groups.title: Earthbenders
groups.def: Every non-Avatar character confirmed on screen to earthbend (including metalbending and lavabending, which are earthbending sub-skills).

groups.title: Red Lotus
groups.def: Named members of the anarchist Red Lotus organization.

groups.title: Metal Clan
groups.def: Characters affiliated with Suyin Beifong's city of Zaofu and its Metal Clan.

groups.title: Beifong Family
groups.def: Toph Beifong's blood descendants, plus Suyin's adopted daughter Kuvira.

groups.title: Republic City Police
groups.def: Officers or chiefs of the Republic City Police shown or named in the show: chiefs Toph, Lin and Saikhan, and Mako, a detective in Book Two. Bolin only joins the force in the post-series Turf Wars comics.

groups.title: Married Couples
groups.def: Characters shown or stated on screen to be married, widowed included: Tenzin and Pema, Tonraq and Senna, Varrick and Zhu Li (who wed in the finale), Suyin (husband Baatar), Raiko (wife Buttercup, on screen in Book Two), Katara (Aang's widow) and Hiroshi (his wife was killed). Unalaq's and Zuko's spouses are never mentioned in the show.

groups.title: Metalbenders
groups.def: Every non-Avatar character confirmed on screen to metalbend. Aiwei raises metal walls in "The Terror Within"; Korra metalbends too but is the Avatar.

groups.title: Heads of State
groups.def: Characters who hold a ruler's title for a nation, tribe or self-governing city in the show: Earth Queen Hou-Ting, King Wu, President Raiko, chiefs Unalaq, Tonraq, Desna and Eska (co-chiefs of the North after Unalaq), Suyin (Zaofu), Kuvira (Earth Empire), and Zuko, "Fire Lord Zuko" in the Book One opening narration.

groups.title: Children of Team Avatar
groups.def: Children of the original series' Team Avatar: Aang and Katara's three (Tenzin, Bumi, Kya) and Toph's two daughters (Lin, Suyin). Zuko's daughter Izumi isn't in this file; Sokka has no children.

groups.title: Earth Empire
groups.def: Characters affiliated with Kuvira's Earth Empire regime in Book Four.

groups.title: Spirits
groups.def: Spirit World residents: the spirits Raava, Vaatu and Bum-Ju, plus Iroh, who lives there as a spirit after his death. Humans who only visit or have a spiritual gift (Korra, Jinora) don't count.

groups.title: Triple Threat Triad
groups.def: Named members of the Triple Threat Triad gang seen on screen (Mako and Bolin are former members from their street-kid days).

groups.title: Fire Ferrets
groups.def: Every member of the Fire Ferrets pro-bending team at some point in Book One.

groups.title: Twins
groups.def: Characters who are one half of a pair of twins.

groups.title: Back from the Original Series
groups.def: Characters from Avatar: The Last Airbender who reappear, now elderly (or as a spirit), in this show.

groups.title: Main villain of a Book
groups.def: The main antagonists of the four books: Amon (One), Unalaq and Vaatu, who merge into the Dark Avatar (Two), Zaheer (Three), Kuvira (Four). Secondary villains (Tarrlok, Hiroshi, Varrick, P'Li, Ming-Hua, Ghazan, Baatar Jr.) don't count.

groups.title: Industrialists
groups.def: The heads of the show's two big companies: Future Industries (Hiroshi Sato, then Asami) and Varrick Global Industries (Varrick, with Zhu Li his right hand and, by the finale, his equal partner).

groups.title: Animal Companions
groups.def: Named, ordinary (non-spirit) animals who appear in the show.

groups.title: Korra's relatives
groups.def: Korra's family: her parents Tonraq and Senna, her uncle Unalaq and her twin cousins Desna and Eska.

groups.title: Debended by Amon
groups.def: Characters whose bending Amon takes away in Book One: Zolt and Shady Shin at the Revelation rally, Tahno, Lin, Tarrlok, and Korra (all but her airbending). Bolin, Mako and Tenzin's family are saved just in time.

groups.title: Died during the show
groups.def: Characters who die during the series' story: Amon and Tarrlok (boat explosion), Unalaq, P'Li, Ming-Hua, Ghazan, Hou-Ting and Hiroshi (Book Four finale). Iroh died before the show; Aiwei is trapped in the Fog of Lost Souls, not killed; Viper's death is comics-only. Destroyed spirits aren't counted, so this group never shares a board with Spirits.

groups.title: Got engaged on screen
groups.def: Characters who become engaged on screen: Kuvira and Baatar Jr. (Book Four), Bolin and Eska (she ties a betrothal necklace on him in Book Two), Varrick and Zhu Li (he proposes in the finale).

groups.title: Airbenders since Harmonic Convergence
groups.def: Former nonbenders who gain airbending after Harmonic Convergence: Bumi, Kai, Opal and Zaheer. Tenzin, Jinora, Ikki and Meelo were born airbenders; Korra is the Avatar.

groups.title: Voiced by Dee Bradley Baker
groups.def: Characters voiced by Dee Bradley Baker in the show (wiki voice credits): the animals Naga, Pabu and Oogi, the spirit Bum-Ju, Tarrlok, and Bumi in his Book One cameo ("Endgame"; Richard Riehle voices him afterwards). Druk has no credited voice.

groups.title: Same name as an ATLA character
groups.def: Characters whose name is the full name of a different character from Avatar: The Last Airbender: Bumi (King Bumi), Kya (Katara's mother), General Iroh (Zuko's uncle Iroh) and Wu (Aunt Wu the fortuneteller). Characters who are the ATLA characters themselves (Katara, Zuko, Toph, Iroh) don't count.
